Honestly, there really aren't any, not on the scale of No Man's Sky, at least.

One of the best space exploration games ever is free, it's called Ur-Quan Masters and you can download it here: http://sc2.sourceforge.net/downloads.php It is an old game that was ported to windows and made freeware, and is best played with a controller. The graphics are similar to Super Nintendo.

For something more modern, Elite: Dangerous is out for PC and coming soon for Xbone and has a comparable space exploration mechanic but its just stars and stellar phenomena that you can explore, there are no planetary landings or alien species.

The recent indie game Interstellaria is quite good but rather limited in scope; it is fun though, and easy to play.

If he's into exploration in general, he may enjoy Miasmata, in which you are stranded on an island and need to use cartography skills to map the island out while evading a weird green cat monster and also cure yourself of a disease. Miasmata is a modern game with attractive graphics, it came out maybe 2 or 3 years ago.

If he likes impossible old games there is Robinson's Requiem, where you are a spaceship crash survivor on a dangerous alien planet. It is almost unplayably difficult, however.

If that sounds kinda like something he would like, consider Albion, which was recently rereleased on www.GOG.com; it is another older game from the 90s and has a similar premise but is much more fun and engaging.

If mobile games like RymdResa are acceptable consider Out There, which is also available on PC. It is a space exploration game with relatively simple mechanics, though it can be somewhat repetitive.

If he is into exploring weird stuff and enjoys reading (a lot of reading) about a strange, unique world I would suggest Sunless Sea. The gameplay is all either text or controlling a ship but the text is excellent and there is nothing quite like it (though honestly it is structurally similar to Ur Quan Masters).

If he enjoys historical exploration the best possible suggestion is definitely Expeditions: Conquistador, a turn based RPG/strategy game where you lead a crew of explorers, soldiers, priests, medics and whatever else through the wilderness of the New World as a Spanish explorer.

If you don't mind getting something unfinished (and depending on how good his PC is), look up Subnautica or Starbound. Subnautica is like Minecraft except in a beautifully rendered alien ocean, and Starbound is like a scifi Terraria. Neither is finished, and probably will not be for a while, but both offer a decent experience even though they are incomplete.

All of these games are exclusive to PC, as far as I know. Console doesn't really cater to these tastes.

Expeditions: Conquistador is a variation on the traditional RPG structure but it is turn based, like a complicated game of chess. Heroes of the Storm is technically a MOBA (Multiplayer Online Battle Arena) game, so I don't know if he meant that was his first time liking a MOBA or maybe he has so little experience with RPGs he thought it was an RPG; either way, I'd avoid it without discussing it with him, better safe than sorry. The game is more strategy/tactics than RPG, really, similar to the recent XCOM game but still, better to go with a sure thing.

Miasmata is actually a totally different type of game, a First Person Exploration/Survival game; it plays more like, say, Minecraft or Skyrim in that you are looking out of your character's eyes as you explore the island; when you look at your map, your character actually pulls out a map and holds it in his hands and looks at it. The interesting thing with Miasmata is you actually triangulate your position using landmarks to fill in your map, kinda like a real explorer/cartographer would do. Unfortunately PC games are largely unavailable in retail stores unless they are really big budget releases so that will not be an option, not at Best Buy or anywhere else.

The good news is that PC games purchased online through services like Steam are instantaneous; basically, it's like buying something on iTunes, you are able to download it immediately. So if you bought it on Steam and gifted it to him he would be able to download it as soon as he accepted the gift (ie, instantaneously).

If you want to give him something physical, however, you could purchase the game through GOG, download it yourself and copy it to DVD and then make a DVD case for him to unwrap, etc. You'd have to be a little arts n crafty to pull that off but you can probably find a decent DVD case picture. A GOG.com account is free and the game itself is only 2.5 gig so it should fit on any DVD (just choose to create a Data DVD when you burn it and include the 3 files that make up the game). The GOG version also gives you wallpaper to download (which would probably be good to make a DVD case and possibly a DVD label as well depending on your resources and how fancy you want to get) and a manual, which you could print out and bind/staple/whatever. Because the GOG version is DRM free he can install it on as many computers as he wants; he doesn't need a GOG account of his own, or to install any special software.

My suggestion would be to go the GOG route: go to www.gog.com, make a free account, purchase Miasmata for 14.99, download all the files, burn them all onto a blank DVD, print out the wallpaper in a size that would fit into a dvd case and slip it into an old DVD case, print out the manual and do the same, combine it all, wrap it up and you're set. If you're not feeling particularly craftsy you can skip all that of course and just burn all the files to a DVD. Depending on your internet connection (and possibly access to a printer) it shouldn't take more than 2 hours, probably less.
